steps.content: You push open the door and walk into the reception room.
Upon hearing you enter, the man in front of you stands up, a big smile on his face. He extends his hand to you.
Thank you for taking the time to meet with me, Chief.
The man is wearing a crumpled trench coat, and his tie has come loose. He looks every bit the typical middle-aged man you'd see around Eastside.
He is courteous, but looks uneasy. Nevertheless, you shake his outstretched hand.
My name is Frank Miller; I'm a clerk from the City Council.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Ah, when I sent the email requesting a visit, I thought: The Chief of the MBCC was the most popular figure these days. My email would probably go unanswered, and I should count myself lucky if I received a rejection email.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: I really lucked out. I can't believe that the Chief of the MBCC, who saved millions of lives in the West District, would agree to meet someone as insignificant as me. You do live up to the name "Heroic Chief."
The man's over-the-top tone and demeanor are making you feel a bit uncomfortable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Thank you, Mr. Frank. That's what I should do.
You check the time on your terminal and decide to put a stop to his cringeworthy praises.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Tell me why you've come.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Sorry, sorry... What you and your Sinners have accomplished in the West District is really, really inspiring! Seeing you in person, I-I just got carried away...
The man adjusts his tie.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Long story short: thanks to you, the number of supporters of our policy has been increasing, and our work is going more smoothly now.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Whose policy? Whose work?
The man hears the doubt in your voice.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Ours...

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: The progressives in the City Council.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: I'm here today to invite you to a hearing scheduled to take place one week from now...

You must have heard about the hearing. It's a public meeting scheduled by the City Council, in response to the recent events that have transpired in the West District. As soon as the news about the hearing was out, it attracted attention from all walks of life in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, you guys want me to... pick sides at this hearing regarding the Executive Committee's dereliction of duty, to declare support for the progressives...

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: No, no, we're not asking you to pick sides. Currently, the majority of the City Council members are, for lack of a better word, conservatives... We know we're no match for them; we wouldn't ask you to make an enemy out of them.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: All you need to do is speak your mind and tell the truth when the time comes.
The man rubs his palms together, looking somewhat uneasy.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: At this juncture, the liberation and welfare of the people of the West District is a sure thing.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: We're not asking you to take our side. We're just hoping you'll stay on the side of the people of the West District. You're on their side, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: I heard that there's another MBCC member who played an active role in the recent events and fared brilliantly. The name is Matilda. If Miss Matilda could choose the side of the people of the West District as well, it would undoubtedly be a huge help!
After his passionate speech, the man gives you a meaningful smile.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Of course, you won't be fighting alone.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: We've won over some of the media outlets that are eligible to attend the hearing, and they'll report the truth. We'll also help hold back pressure from the conservatives.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: On top of that, we've had some funds ready, for investigation purposes. You can make use of them whenever you need.
The man produces a black card from his pocket and slides it over the tabletop.
Without saying a word, you slide the card back.
Surprise registers in the man's eyes. Finally, you speak.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I will attend the hearing.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: I've heard so much about how noble the Chief of the MBCC is. Today, I've seen it with my own eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for Matilda...
You look the man in the eye.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm her superior, yes, but I still need to ask for her opinion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She's a former member of the Executive Committee, after all. Whether she wants to choose sides at this point is her decision entirely.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: Of course, of course.
The man can no longer keep joy from his face. He makes himself look slightly more presentable before extending his hand to you once again.

steps.speaker: Frank
steps.content: I have faith in Miss Matilda. She'll make the choice she believes to be right.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: So, you've given them your word?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I only promised to tell the truth.
Despite the fact that you haven't had much contact with Matilda since she arrived at the Bureau, her meticulous and efficient working style has left a strong impression on you.
Although she can come across as rigid and formal—a result of her strict adherence to rules, she's a very reliable adjutant professionally.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But I'm not going to speak for the benefit of the progressives, even though their offer is indeed tempting.
A large amount of money, political quid pro quo... You explain the progressives' offer to Matilda.
Throughout your explanation, the neatly dressed former Executive Committee adjutant listens without uttering a word.
When you're finished, she ponders for a moment before making her comments.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: If I may speak frankly, Chief, this invitation might not be what you think it is.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: It is... a trap.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes, a trap.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: That the progressives in the City Council will make a move after the Executive Committee's debacle is to be expected. But, to put it bluntly, they don't have what it takes to pull off anything major.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Political quid pro quo... well, that's possible, given that they hold 8% of the seats on the City Council.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: But the funds...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I don't know the exact amount. But the card you just mentioned... if I'm not mistaken, it was issued by a private bank that has business dealings with many big figures in Eastside's political and business circles.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: They only provide one-on-one services, known for their ability to guarantee complete confidentiality for their clients. Whether your assets are gray or black, they can make them clean.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Unfortunately for the councilors from the progressive wing, their private assets might not be large enough to qualify them for cards from this bank.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you saying...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes. I'm certain that this Frank is not a member of the progressive wing.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: These so-called progressives appeared on the scene several decades ago. But ten years ago, they were completely defeated, and they've never been on center stage since.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Today, they exist on the periphery of the City Council, serving as a "necessary opposing voice." They owe their existence to the mercy of those in power.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The Executive Committee's debacle represents an opportunity for them, one that they must seize. Unfortunately for them, this kind of game...
Matilda looks at you with a smile on her face.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: It's simply out of their league.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your understanding of the workings of the City Council far exceeds my expectations.
Matilda knows too much for an adjutant of a frontline Executive Officer.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If it weren't for you, I would still be kept in the dark.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: It's what I should do as your subordinate.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: You don't deal with them often. It's hard to know the truth without sufficient information.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Add that to what this Frank did... The Speaker's faction has always been good at using these little tricks... This is why I'm so sure of my conclusion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Speaker's faction?
The conclusion, so casually made by Matilda, confuses you even more.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're saying the Speaker, leader of the conservative wing of the City Council, wants me to truthfully present the situation in the West District, to make statements that are harmful to them?
Matilda picks up on your confusion and goes on to explain:

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes. Although it seems contradictory, the logic is not hard to grasp.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Like I said earlier, this is a trap, but you're not the target, Chief.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I am.
Matilda pauses for a moment. Looking you in the eye, she continues:

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Bernadette Cavendish... You must've heard of this name, I presume?
You have. You're not in the habit of seeking out news about the political scene, but you've heard this name mentioned here and there, through this channel or that.
The de facto leader of the Cavendish family, a star member of the City Council, a role model for the women in Eastside... and a popular candidate for the Speaker's seat in next year's election.
And then the full name of Matilda springs to your mind. You first came across the name while skimming through her file when she was transferred to the MBCC.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Matilda Cavendish...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes, that's my full name. Councilor Bernadette, the current City Secretary...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: She is my aunt.
Things start to make sense now.
When the West District Reconstruction Committee was dissolved following its failure, many of its members faced dire consequences.
As a former member, Matilda was swiftly transferred to the MBCC, the safest place a Sinner can be.
And now, the consequences have come looking for her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, the Speaker's faction intends to use you against your aunt, right?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Yes.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The real threat to the Speaker has never been the progressives, but his overly active "subordinate" who has announced her candidacy.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Few things pose a threat to Ms. Bernadette. Unfortunately, due to a combination of many uncontrollable factors, I seem to have become the only weak point that the Speaker can take advantage of.
Matilda looks up at you, her eyes filled with apology.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Chief, I'm sorry for getting you involved...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you're worried about the possible adverse effect on Councilor Bernadette, I can make a joint statement with you at the hearing, cutting ties with all factions...
Before you can finish, Matilda shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: It won't work.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I'm a member of the Cavendish family. Once I stand behind the podium to say my piece, everything I have done, everything I have said... it will be used by the other conservatives to attack Ms. Bernadette.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: A relative of a conservative councilor openly expressing sympathy for the West District... This is likely to become the biggest stain on Ms. Bernadette's political career...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I could claim that I did what I did in the West District because I was forced to. This would possibly minimize the damage to our family's interests, but...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: After all I have been through, I can't, in good conscience, bring myself to lie.
Matilda lowers her head. Her lips are moving, as if she has something more to say, but nothing comes out.
The fact that Matilda is in so much agony can only mean one thing...
She has decided to attend the hearing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're right. We've been through it all together...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I don't know much about politics, but I can play tricks too.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can get you a medical report saying that you were critically injured during an operation in the West District and almost died.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Or I can tell them that you've been sent to a satellite town for an important task.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: My point is, as long as you're not available, they can't use you to attack Councilor Bernadette...
Your attempt at humor works, at least for a moment. Matilda's furrowed brow relaxes slightly.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Haha...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Even if I disappeared from DisCity, it wouldn't really help the situation.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The Speaker's faction has set their plan in motion. They're going to pull out all the stops to turn the spotlight on me, whether I attend the hearing or not.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I won't let that stop me from speaking up for the West District. If not me, who else will?
You understand Matilda's choice.

You understand why she is choosing to speak up for the West District, even though she can't really change anything or weaken the conservatives' position in the City Council, and anything she says and does can be used against her family.
Since the very beginning, she has never considered not attending the hearing. She is anxious to convey everything she saw and learned in the West District to Eastside.
Her mind is made up. Matilda looks back at you with a determined look in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I won't run away. I must attend the hearing.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Even if the Speaker's faction has considered everything, there's one thing they got wrong.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I, the "pawn," am the only variable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You have thought of a countermeasure?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I wouldn't call it a countermeasure, but... I want to give it a try.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Ms. Bernadette must've known about the Speaker's faction's move, but so far, the Cavendish family hasn't made any public announcement to sever ties with me.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Which means that Ms. Bernadette believes that I'll make the right choice, even though it may not be a choice the family would want me to make. But I will never let my aunt and the rest of my family down.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I'll do everything I can before the hearing to find a way to turn the situation around.
Matilda takes a deep breath. Her expression becomes even more determined.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: All right... I understand.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: By the way, is there anything I can help you with?
Matilda thinks for a moment, and then gives you a somewhat shy smile; she rarely smiles.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: If it's not too much to ask...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Could I use your office for a while?
